episodes.212781: A frontal boundary began the day nearly stationary near the Florida/Georgia border on the morning of the 2nd, progressing towards south of the region by that same evening. Widespread stratiform rainfall accompanied the front, with some embedded thunderstorms across northeast FL. Modest instability ahead of the front, as well as moderate to strong wind shear associated with the base of an upper level trough, supported isolated severe thunderstorms despite convection occurring during the first half of the day.
episodes.213257: A cluster of strong storms moved across the coastal waters with a measured wind gust of 34 knots on Saint George Island.
episodes.213579: A line of showers and storms south of a stationary boundary draped over the Florida panhandle produced gusty winds over Cedar Key and Tampa Bay area waters.
episodes.213815: A stationary frontal boundary was draped across the northern Gulf Coast beneath nearly zonal midlevel flow. At the same time, a series of upper-level impulses moved through the region. A weak surface low developed along the boundary during the afternoon hours and supported renewed thunderstorms over the southeast Louisiana coastal waters. The storms moved east across waters south of Cocodrie and Venice and produced several severe marine wind gusts.
episodes.213816: Convection associated with a departing frontal system from the previous day remained over the far offshore waters southeast of Venice early on May 2nd. One thunderstorm produced a severe marine wind gust before the remaining activity moved out of the local waters.
episodes.214320: Thunderstorms along and ahead of a cold front produced strong to severe wind gusts along the coast.
episodes.214321: Thunderstorms along and ahead of a cold front produced severe wind gusts in Brevard County.
